title: High protein chocolate mousse (Gelatine)
summary: Gelatine, cacao and 0% yogurt blended until it is pale and foaming, then set. A whole bowl of it comes to about 47 g of protein for under 400 calories, and most of what you are eating is air.

time.note: Plus about 2 hours setting in the fridge.

nutrition_per_serving.note: The whole bowl including the toppings. Assumes a 0% fat Greek style yogurt at around 10 g protein per 100 g; a thinner 0% natural yogurt drops the protein by roughly 9 g.

ingredients.note: The only setting agent, and it is also what traps the air the blender whips in. Powder, not leaf: it dissolves straight into boiling water. If sheets are all you have, bloom about 6 of them in cold water first, squeeze them out, then stir them into the hot liquid - dry sheets dropped into boiling water will not hydrate evenly.

ingredients.qty: 200 g 0% fat, plus 30 g to top

ingredients.note: Melted into the hot gelatine water. It is here for the fat and the depth - the cacao is doing the actual chocolate flavour.

steps: Stir the gelatine into 300 ml of boiling water until every grain has gone. Undissolved gelatine sets into rubbery threads you cannot blend out later.
Add the dark chocolate to the hot liquid and stir until it melts.

Tip that into a blender with the yogurt, cacao, whey and sweetener, and blend until it is pale and foaming. The blending is the recipe: it is what builds the volume, and the gelatine is only there to hold the foam once it cools.
Blend it while the gelatine mix is still warm. Left to cool on the counter it starts to gel, and gelatine that has begun setting will not whip up.
Pour into a bowl and refrigerate about 2 hours, until set.
Top with the extra yogurt and the raspberries.
tips: Work quickly once the gelatine is dissolved. This is the opposite of most set desserts, where you cool the liquid before it meets the yogurt - here cooling it first costs you the aeration.
Blend for longer than feels sensible. The difference between a dense set pudding and an actual mousse is entirely how much air went in.
A wide shallow bowl sets faster than a deep one, and it keeps the aerated top layer intact.
It deflates a little overnight. Best eaten the day you make it.
health_notes: Nearly 47 g of protein for under 400 calories is a very good ratio, but about 9 g of it is gelatine, which is an incomplete protein and low in tryptophan - it is worth less to you than the same weight of whey or dairy. The rest, from the yogurt and the powder, is complete.

source.title: Low Calorie High Volume Protein Mousse (INSANE)
source.adapted: Ingredients and quantities are from the pinned comment. The video supplies the method the comment omits: everything goes through a blender rather than being stirred, which is what creates the volume, and it sets in the fridge for about two hours. The comment lists a generic sweetener; erythritol is recorded because 1-2 tsp only makes sense for a bulking sweetener, and that quantity of stevia would be inedible. Nutrition recalculated at roughly 390 calories and 48 g protein against the stated 371 and 47, close enough that the gap is brand variation. Carbs, fat and fibre were not given by the source and are estimated here.
